source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

profile.reading: DartPoints own company site describes a strategy of delivering enterprise grade colocation, cloud, and managed infrastructure services to communities outside the largest United States metros, operating in Tier 2 and Tier 3 regional markets. The company began operations in the early 2000s and received a strategic growth investment from NOVA Infrastructure in 2025. DartPoints is headquartered at 1601 Elm Street, Suite 3650, Dallas, Texas. The company own site lists 11 facilities including Baton Rouge, Louisiana (2 facilities) and Shreveport, Louisiana; Cincinnati and Dublin, Ohio; Columbus, Indiana; Asheville, North Carolina; and Columbia, Greenville, Charleston, and Spartanburg, South Carolina, matching every state where this registry lists a DartPoints facility. The South Carolina registry row listed as Ladson likely corresponds to the Charleston area market named on the company site, since Ladson is a suburb of Charleston, though this specific building was not individually confirmed. The company emphasizes AI ready, high density infrastructure, 99.999 percent uptime, and SOC 2 Type II compliance. No building specific address or individual MW figures for this particular registry row were located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
DartPoints Greenville in Greenville, South Carolina, publishes 2.5 MW of IT capacity, operated by DartPoints.

At 10 kW per rack, a common enterprise colocation density, that load supports roughly 250 racks. At 40 kW per rack, a density closer to AI training workloads, it supports roughly 62 racks. The operator has not published a per-rack power envelope, so neither figure is the operator's own claim, only what the published megawattage implies under each assumption.

No compliance certifications are published for DartPoints Greenville. That does not mean none exist, only that this site's dataset, built from the operator's own facility page, does not list any, which limits what regulated workloads a reader could confirm the facility is qualified to host.

South Carolina has 4 facilities mapped in this site's dataset, of which 4 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 6.6 MW. DartPoints Greenville contributes 2.5 MW of that total. At that published size it is a small facility relative to what frontier AI training infrastructure requires, which now runs into the tens or hundreds of megawatts, though it may still support inference workloads or smaller-scale AI applications.
